terra.problem: The guest-list joke does not make sense: someone on the last page is still on the list.
The psalm does not say whether the singer is whispering.
The hat joke has no clear connection to splendor or the throne’s foundation.
The kitchen hiding joke makes light of the fire consuming the LORD’s foes.
The timer comparison does not clearly explain why a timer would shake on a bad day.
The psalm says the mountains melt like wax; it does not say that the biggest, most stubborn things on earth give way.
The explanation states what the singer wants listeners to feel, but the text does not give that intention.
The explanation repeats the answer several times without adding insight or much of Papa Dorin’s personality.
The psalm says all the peoples see His glory, but it does not say they see it by looking up at the sky.
The explanation adds that the idols cannot hold up as an explanation for the worshipers’ shame. The verse does not give that reason.
The cookie-money joke makes light of boasting in idols, the serious sin addressed in the verse.
The parchment-paper joke compares the LORD’s position to Papa Dorin hiding behind a stack, placing Papa in God’s role for the joke.
The explanation mostly repeats the command and ends with a generic observation, without adding insight or much personality.
